title: Ticketmaster
summary: Sell a fixed inventory of seats to a flash crowd without double-booking: a virtual waiting room, short-lived seat reservations with TTL locks, payment, and an event page served from cache.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Browse and search events; view the seat map with availability
Reserve seats for a few minutes, pay, receive tickets
Never sell the same seat twice (strong consistency on booking)
Survive on-sale spikes: millions of users for ~50k seats
Browsing can be eventually consistent and heavily cached

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Demand exceeds supply by 100×+. The design problem is admission control and contention, not raw throughput.

GET  /events/{id}                         -> event + venue (CDN cached)
GET  /events/{id}/seats                   -> availability map (cached ~1-5 s)
POST /events/{id}/reservations  {seat_ids[]}  -> {reservation_id, expires_at} | 409
POST /reservations/{id}/checkout {payment_token, idempotency_key} -> {booking_id}

head: Table
Key
Fields
rows: status: available | reserved | sold, reservation_id, reserved_until, version

blocks.caption: Admission control in front of a strongly consistent booking path

sections.title: Deep dive: reserving a seat without double-booking

cols.title: Pessimistic: SELECT … FOR UPDATE
pros: Simple and correct within one DB
cons: Locks held during user think time block others — never hold DB locks across a 10-minute checkout

cols.title: Status + expiry column (optimistic)
pros: UPDATE seats SET status='reserved', reserved_until=now()+10m WHERE id=? AND (status='available' OR reserved_until<now())
cons: Need a sweeper or lazy expiry

cols.title: Distributed lock with TTL (Redis SET NX PX)
cons: The DB must still be the source of truth at checkout

items: At checkout: in one transaction, verify the reservation still owns the seats and flip them to `sold`; only then capture payment (or authorise first, capture after).
Use an idempotency key on checkout so a double-click can't book twice.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: A reservation is a conditional write with an expiry, not a held lock. Expired holds become available again without any cleanup job being on the critical path.

sections.title: Deep dive: the virtual waiting room

items.title: Enqueue
items.text: At on-sale time users hitting the event are given a position (randomised for those who arrived before start).

items.title: Admit
items.text: A controller admits N users per second based on booking-service capacity, issuing signed, short-lived access tokens.

items.title: Notify
items.text: Clients poll or hold an SSE/WebSocket connection to see their position and get the token.

items.title: Enforce
items.text: The booking service rejects requests without a valid token — the queue is the rate limiter.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Serve the seat map from cache with a few seconds' staleness; the conditional reserve write is what guarantees correctness, so a stale map only means an occasional 409.

items: Shard seats by event_id: one hot event lives on one shard, which is fine because the waiting room caps its write rate.
Bots: CAPTCHA at queue entry, per-account limits, purchase caps.
Payment provider slow → reservations expire mid-checkout: extend the hold when payment starts.
General-admission events: model as an inventory counter decremented atomically instead of per-seat rows.

cols.title: Eventual consistency for browsing
cons: Users sometimes see seats that are already gone

items.title: Scope
items.text: Browse, reserve, pay; on-sale spikes; no double booking.

items.title: HLD
items.text: CDN + event service; booking service + DB.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Conditional reserve with TTL; waiting room.

items.title: Scale
items.text: Shard by event, bots, payment timeouts.

items.q: What happens if Redis loses a lock?
items.a: The DB conditional write at checkout is the real guard; Redis only reduces contention.

items.q: How do you show live availability?
items.a: Publish seat-status changes to a channel; clients subscribed via SSE get deltas, or just poll a cached map.

items.q: How do you keep the waiting room fair?
items.a: Randomise early arrivals, issue one position per verified account, expire inactive positions.

items: Waiting room = admission control + signed tokens.
Browse from cache; correctness from the write.
